title: Measuring ROI on AI-assisted development
question: What does AI-assisted development cost, what value does it deliver, and can we credibly attribute the difference?
summary: ROI requires both the incremental cost of AI-assisted work and its incremental value against a comparable baseline. Local Copilot stores report consumption and some work context, not monetary cost, developer time saved or delivered value. The live measurements below show how much reported usage can be linked to work; they are ROI readiness indicators, not ROI. A deterministic PR join, verified delivery and quality outcomes, billing and human effort data, and a comparable baseline are needed before calculating a return.

linkMethods.name: Tool-provided link
linkMethods.method: The tool reports which work belongs to the session.
linkMethods.example: A cloud session points directly to its pull request. A pull request merely mentioned in local records is still just a mention until checked.

linkMethods.name: Exact match
linkMethods.method: One clear match using repository, commit and time.
linkMethods.example: Match a commit to a checked pull request. Reused branches, forks or several matching pull requests need a choice, not a guess.

linkMethods.name: Likely match
linkMethods.method: Related work at the same time, but no exact link.
linkMethods.example: The same account worked in the repository during the change, and edited some of the same files. This suggests a link; it does not prove one.

linkMethods.name: Estimated share
linkMethods.method: Divide an amount in proportion to recorded usage.
linkMethods.example: If a work item accounts for one quarter of the billed credits for the account, day and model, estimate one quarter of the charge after discounts. This is not a measured work-item bill.

linkMethods.name: Not linked
linkMethods.example: Keep the usage visible rather than guessing or dropping it.

invariants: Count each AI request once, using its stable ID. Some tools report totals for a whole agent run; never add a run summary to the requests it includes. Check the correct credit field for each tool and version.
Do not add overlapping sources. For matching measurements and periods, choose one source or use the larger value, not their sum. Record where the number came from and what was included.
Unknown is not zero; show how many requests include credit counts alongside the reported credit total.
Credits = nano-AIU / 1,000,000,000, including Agent Tasks usage.amount; sum nano values before dividing. No token-to-currency estimate without an explicit, labelled rate.
Do not assign more than 100% of a session’s usage to work. Keep any usage without a supported link visible.
Local records are not a bill. Compare recorded usage with the bill for the same account and period, using credits before discounts. Keep discounts and final charges separate.
Do not read prompts or responses. Protect account IDs before saving or exporting, and keep tool server names hidden unless an approved lookup is available.
Credits, reused input and pull request mentions do not prove savings or business value. Show costs, results and the comparison with similar work separately.
Token counts may cover only some requests; show which ones reported each count. Input reuse uses requests with both valid input and reused-input counts. A missing count stays unknown, not zero.

reconciliation.source: Explicit Recipe billing read: /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage, /enterprises/{enterprise}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage or /users/{username}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage. Requires billing access to the paying account.
reconciliation.grain: Paying account × day in UTC × GitHub account × product/SKU × model; preserve the request filters because each usageItems row may omit part of this context.
requirements: Organisation ai_credits_used is user-level consumption, not invoicing and not a model/feature/surface breakdown; reconcile it only at its published grain.
Use the billing entity that pays for the seat. Personal endpoints exclude organisation-managed seats; organisation/enterprise access requires the appropriate administrative permissions.

Compare captured native users for one completed UTC day, Copilot product and exact model names, per local source. Inferred owners are excluded. Local metadata does not prove the selected account paid for those calls.
Keep gross, discount and net quantities/amounts separate. Preserve API units and pricePerUnit; never turn local credits into currency with a guessed rate.
Store filters and returned scope metadata, retrieval time, coverage and a stable ledger key. Do not add overlapping per-day/user/model queries or duplicate local sources.
Report signed differences and unmatched usage explicitly. Missing local data is not zero usage. Unsupported units fail visibly; failed reads never retain an old report as current.
Billing accrues independently of merge. Its reports have no PR, issue, branch or session IDs.
reconciliation.allocationPolicy: Estimated work cost is a proportional share, not measured pull request or session billing: charge after discounts × recorded account’s work credits / credits on the bill, per model. Keep unexplained charges separate and do not estimate a share when recorded credits exceed billed credits.

evidence.label: Checked online
evidence.description: Confirmed by GitHub or Azure Boards when you ask to check delivery.

evidence.label: Mentioned
evidence.description: The agent mentioned a pull request, issue or commit. A mention does not prove ownership or delivery.

evidence.label: Branch name
evidence.description: The work-item number comes from the branch name. It has not been checked online.

evidence.label: Local record
evidence.description: Recorded on this machine: sessions, AI requests, credits, branches and commits.

convention.branch: The work item is the first token after the last slash: prefix/AB123-slug is Azure Boards work item 123; prefix/123-slug is GitHub issue 123 in the same repository.
convention.hook: Opt-in commit-msg hook that adds a Refs: AB#123 or Refs: #123 trailer from the branch name when the message does not already reference it, so Azure Boards and GitHub create their own links.

guardrails: Verification runs only when requested and sends repository, branch and PR, issue or work-item numbers plus first-activity timestamps for historical assignment snapshots.

Queries select state, date, type, commit and assignment metadata, including GitHub logins and Azure Boards account IDs/display names. Titles, descriptions, commit messages, comments and email fields are never requested.
GitHub uses the signed-in gh CLI; Azure Boards uses az account get-access-token or AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT. Tokens stay in memory and are never logged, returned or stored.
Credits stay per source. A cycle that spans the CLI/app store and VS Code shows both values, never a sum.
Reported credits per merged PR are consumption, not cost or value.
Measured user.name consumption, inferred historical-owner/PR-author allocation and unattributed usage remain separate. Current assignment is never backdated and conflicting owners stay unattributed.
Provider identities are distinct unless explicitly linked. Matching names, email addresses, devices and branch prefixes never establish a person.

outcomes.name: PR-reference coverage
outcomes.measure: % of reported credits in sessions with a repository, branch and recorded PR reference; not verified delivery or value

outcomes.name: Work-context coverage
outcomes.measure: % of reported credits on model calls with resolved repository context, including trace-only links; not verified work ownership

outcomes.name: Credit coverage
outcomes.measure: % of model calls that report credits

outcomes.name: Actor coverage
outcomes.measure: % of reported credits on model calls attributed to a user.name (opt-in identity capture); a join key to per-user organisation data, not a productivity measure

outcomes.name: Cost per delivered change
outcomes.measure: Credits per merged PR, per work-item type

outcomes.name: AI-assisted share
outcomes.measure: % of merged pull requests linked directly by the tool or by an exact match

outcomes.name: Cache-read share
outcomes.measure: Cache-read / input tokens over calls reporting both valid counts, with paired-call coverage; usage mix, not time or money saved

outcomes.name: Speed
outcomes.measure: Local latency/TTFT fields exist but are not rendered here; PR lead time vs a matched baseline needs verified PR data

outcomes.name: Quality
outcomes.measure: Acceptance/survival require the telemetry feed this canvas does not read; reviews, CI, reverts and verified task delivery require external joins

outcomes.name: Billed AI cost
outcomes.measure: Match reported consumption with billing gross AI-credit quantity at the same user/day/model scope; retain discounts/net billed amounts, seats and infrastructure separately

outcomes.name: Human effort and rework
outcomes.measure: Developer time spent prompting, reviewing, correcting and maintaining delivered work vs comparable non-AI work

outcomes.name: Incremental return
outcomes.measure: (Valued incremental benefit − AI investment) / AI investment; include incremental spend and oversight, avoid double-counting time savings, and use a comparable baseline

gaps.title: Usage may not name a work item
gaps.consequence: Local records can stop at a branch or commit. VS Code supplies no work-item number; CLI/app records include one only when the agent mentions it.
gaps.mitigation: Use work-item numbers in branch names and check related pull requests online. Keep usage without a link visible.

gaps.title: Cloud usage API is still a preview
gaps.consequence: GitHub can report credits for a cloud session, but the API may change. These are usage counts, not charges after discounts.
gaps.mitigation: Keep the session and pull request IDs, check the response format, and compare with the bill separately.

gaps.title: Daily reports omit session IDs
gaps.consequence: Organization user totals do not identify sessions or show usage by model and Copilot tool.
gaps.mitigation: Compare daily account totals only. Use the billing report for model detail, and label any work-level cost as an estimate.

gaps.title: The user account may be missing
gaps.consequence: CLI/app session rows hold no account. An anonymous tracking ID is not a GitHub username. VS Code records the account only when enabled.
gaps.mitigation: Enable account recording with consent. Check account links before comparing reports; never guess from a computer name or email.

gaps.title: Some requests have no session
gaps.consequence: A request may still have repository context without enough information to identify its session.
gaps.mitigation: Use the matching context available at the time. Do not invent sessions or drop requests that cannot be linked.

gaps.title: VS Code has two harnesses
gaps.consequence: The Local harness uses agent-traces.db. The Copilot Agent Host harness uses agent-host-traces.db, which is off by default.
gaps.mitigation: Set up recording for the harness you use. Keep the two sources separate and preserve any existing external collector.

gaps.title: Older clients under-reported activity
gaps.consequence: Some older editor versions counted too little agent work or labelled it as CLI usage. The missing history was not restored.
gaps.mitigation: Use fixed clients (VS Code 1.139+) and mark affected periods. A lower count does not necessarily mean less work.

gaps.title: The same usage can appear twice
gaps.consequence: Adding overlapping sources can count a request twice. Comparing different time periods can also give misleading totals.
gaps.mitigation: Match stable request IDs and keep one copy. If the overlap cannot be resolved, show the sources separately.

gaps.title: Build and deployment results are not linked
gaps.consequence: A merged change does not tell us whether it built successfully or reached production.
gaps.mitigation: Link build and deployment runs using the repository and commit.

gaps.title: Some requests omit credit counts
gaps.consequence: A missing credit count is unknown, not a free request.
gaps.mitigation: Show how many requests include credit counts, alongside the total credits reported.

gaps.title: A missing token count may not be zero
gaps.consequence: Some tools leave out zero cache or reasoning counts; others do not report them at all.
gaps.mitigation: Show which requests supplied each count. Treat missing values as unknown unless the source explicitly documents otherwise.

gaps.title: Tool server names may be hidden
gaps.consequence: A hidden server name can prevent grouping tool usage by supplier.
gaps.mitigation: Keep the reported ID. Add a readable name only from an approved lookup list.

gaps.title: Different tools use different field names
gaps.consequence: Several field names may describe the same value.
gaps.mitigation: Use checked field mappings and keep the source/version. Do not add alternate names as if they were different usage.

priorArt.name: bear-in-mind
priorArt.proved: Metering from VS Code OTel file feed, agent-traces.db, the Agent Host's agent-host-traces.db (Copilot Agent Host harness, Copilot runtime traces only) and transcripts; cost/speed/quality dashboard with retained-trace credits by model, repository, user, caller and reasoning effort, and session repository and user labels.
priorArt.learned: Count only chat spans; dedupe by span ID; metrics vs spans use max not sum; credits = nano-AIU / 1e9; token share is not credit share; user.name, like repository, sits on invoke_agent spans and must be inherited by chat spans.

priorArt.name: agentic-sdlc-prototypes-patterns
priorArt.proved: OTLP receiver, CLI session-store ingestion, ELK documents with cost/speed/quality groups, pseudonymised developer_id.
priorArt.learned: Spans rarely carried credits then; the CLI store was the reliable cost source; repository must be copied from invoke_agent to chat spans.

priorArt.name: copilot-insights (hackathon)
priorArt.proved: Relational schema joining OTel spans, metrics and events with CLI llm_calls by session.
priorArt.learned: Repo/branch/commit exist, but no PR join was built.

priorArt.name: vscode-insights (hackathon)
priorArt.proved: Copilot SDK instrumentation (assistant.usage, subagent.*, skill.invoked, quota snapshots) into one records table.
priorArt.learned: Stable call keys like sdk:<sessionId>:call:<apiCallId>; account checked against the signed-in login.

verification.claim: copilot_chat.copilot_usage_nano_aiu is emitted on VS Code chat spans
verification.note: genAiAttributes.ts in microsoft/vscode extensions/copilot; present on 985 of 988 local chat spans on 19 October 2026.

Carried inside the copilot_chat.request.options JSON blob, not a dedicated attribute.

verification.claim: VS Code identity capture: user.name on agent invocation spans; process.user.name and host.name as resource attributes
verification.note: VS Code 1.140 release notes and otelIdentity.ts in microsoft/vscode extensions/copilot: off by default; user.name is the GitHub session account label; a managed policy overrides COPILOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_IDENTITY and the setting; agent-traces.db persists span attributes only. microsoft/vscode#337413 closed on 6 October 2026; VS Code 1.141 governs Agent Host identity through managed telemetry.capture.identity.

verification.claim: VS Code Copilot Agent Host harness uses a separate Agent Host OTel pipeline
verification.note: Agent Host OTEL.md and VS Code 1.141/1.142 notes: chat.agentHost.otel.* settings, runtime spans with service.name=github-copilot, agent-host-traces.db only in opt-in DB mode. Neither VS Code build on the measured machine had created it.

verification.claim: Managed OTel capture classes, including Identity
verification.note: GitHub's OTel guide (13 October 2026): identity, prompts, responses, tool arguments, tool output and policy detail, independently enabled in CLI, the app and VS Code Agent Host sessions. The VS Code Local harness supports identity and the legacy content setting only.

verification.claim: VS Code user.name equals the usage metrics user_login
verification.note: Both should be the GitHub login; not tested against an organisation export.

verification.claim: Copilot CLI OTel span, metric and environment-variable names
verification.note: Primary CLI reference documents COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH; invoke_agent/chat/execute_tool; gen_ai.* and github.copilot.*. github.copilot.cost is a multiplier; use the documented root-span nano_aiu aggregation, not VS Code's mapping. It still lists gen_ai.client.operation.* metrics, which the semantic conventions renamed to gen_ai.client.inference.* on 6 October 2026.

verification.claim: VS Code Copilot Agent Host harness sessions in the CLI/app session store, and their exported credit attribute
verification.note: Expected to follow the shared runtime (root github.copilot.nano_aiu); not captured on the measured machine.
Both are service request IDs; equivalence not tested.
Primary usage-based billing docs include cloud agent and define one AI credit as USD 0.01. Premium requests remain for eligible existing annual plans; do not mix billing regimes.
Both are in the primary CLI command reference. They are soft limits, not a hard spending guarantee.

verification.claim: CLI limits reset grain and minimum for the installed runtime
verification.note: The command reference says per response, while the session-limit guide says entire interactive session and a 30-credit minimum; both still disagree on 19 October 2026. Pin the runtime and verify reset/overshoot behaviour before promising semantics.

verification.claim: Enterprise-managed OTel export and cost-centre budgets
verification.note: Primary OTel and organisation billing docs describe enforced telemetry settings and cost-centre budgets for additional charges after pooled credits are exhausted. This is capability evidence, not verification of an account's configuration.

verification.claim: Per-session cloud-agent cost via Agent Tasks REST
verification.note: Session objects document usage.type (ai_credits or premium_requests), usage.amount (nano units for AI credits) and model; public preview. A read-only test returned AI-credit usage for 28 of 33 cloud sessions in the last 30 days. Schema stability is unverified.

verification.claim: Usage metrics undercounted SDK-based IDE agent activity
verification.note: GitHub changelog, 6 October 2026: fixed from VS Code 1.139; affected activity is not backfilled and some was counted as Copilot CLI. Billing unaffected.
